correctness.rationale: For q=4 and three transmitted symbols, each 3-word has at most three distinct length-2 deletion descendants, so five words cannot cover all 16 ordered received pairs. The displayed six-word code gives a partition. Directly inspected exact mask representation M(a,b,c) and complete six-subset DP (64 possible triples), and independently implemented capacity-pruned increasing-sextuple and 24 global symbol permutations times reversal; found 644 optimal covers, 120 disjoint-shadow, 524 overlapping, and 21 orbits: 8*1 + 12*3 + 24*9 + 48*8 = 644. The capacity bound at depths 3,4,5 is 16-3(6-k), so pruning is exhaustive. Every counted codebook is an unordered set with distinct words; duplicate deletion positions are collapsed. This is a finite exhaustive proof only for q=4,n=3, not a general alphabet formula.
